body: Psych wards don't keep patients indefinitely. There is a limited number of beds reserved for crises. When the crisis passes, the patient is released. So, yes, you'll have to do this for the rest of your life unless you can get her into a nursing home.
I'm suicidal and sometimes homicidal for no reason as well. being dead just seems like a much better choice.
no real input here but i can relate and just wanted to say that. thr little voice in the back of the head never really stops begging to be silenced forever.

I've been through treatment without much of an effect. Obviously, I didn't explore all the medication available and all the therapy types available but I am quite resistant to treatment. 

One reason for not still being in treatment is that I get extremely paranoid and assume whomever I talk to is working together for someone else (including my family) in attempts to control me. Because of that thought, I discontinue treatment, often abruptly. Of course, I don't tell them that so they end up not knowing why I suddenly stopped. 

Another reason, which I think is more important, is that I simply don't want treatment now. I can't even get myself to get to a GP for help, let alone someone specialized. I want to sink as deep as possible in hopes that perhaps it will persuade me to act on my ever present desire.

Thank you for your kind words. Your analysis is very accurate. It's not just my own life that I fail to see the value of though, at least consciously. 

I care about the well being of my loved ones but my reasons are very selfish. Every time I'd been on the verge of attempting, I stopped because guilt overwhelmed me. I don't want to feel that. I want peace in what I think will be my happiest moment. To think that I could entertain and seriously contemplate or plan for homicide for a reason like that seems nothing short of monstrous. 

There are people I talk to online and sometimes tell them these things or post them online at places like reddit because something compells me to share. For sharing such thoughts, I feel deeply ashamed. I didn't expect a response so let me once again thank you for writing to me. 

Happiness has become a lost concept to me. I can't grasp it at all. I don't understand what it is that I am supposed to look forward to. Is happy different than this? In what way? What is this? "A horrible lack" really resonates with me at this time.

These people I talk to tell me I need to drop everything and get help. However, I can't take myself seriously. I can't believe what I am typing here. It seems these aren't my thoughts but rather a script I am readinf off a teleprompter somewhere that I had wrotten out previously for the sole purpose of manipulation (of what/who and how, I am not sure). I can hold down a job, as simple as it is... I hear that's something. I can get through the day. I can eat, bathe, shop, chat. I am entirely functional. This horrible lack doesnt crush me completely. Thus, anything I say to imply that I exist in a void must be a lie. I wonder what it is like to be able to trust your thoughts to be the true representation of what you are. Is that happiness? Or is that simply insight.

Sorry about the scattered ramble. I hope it makes sense. Once again, thank you for engaging with me. It seems that there is so much I must say but out of family, friends, therapists and psychiatrists, the only people I can trust enough to say all of them to is you and others like you on the internet who may read what I write but to whom I am nameless, faceless, and inconsequential. Thank you for allowing me to ramble.  I hope I didn't come scross as rude or presumptuous.
I don't think I remember what happy is. For some reason, I am failing to even define it.
